title: RecentActionsV1
description: GET /recent-actions (UX-35): the caller's bills with an action in Congress inside the window, newest first. A bill is the caller's when they voted Yea, Nay or Abstain on it (never an Updates dismissal from app 1.0 or 1.1) or watch it, on either member of a companion group. One row per bill (a companion group is one bill), at most 50. Only the caller's own vote is ever in it: no count, tally or other user's vote.

generatedAt.description: When the server built the list.

windowDays.description: How many days back the actions reach (30 today): an action dated on or after that many Eastern calendar days before generatedAt's.

items.description: Newest action first, then by title. Empty when the caller has no bill with an action in the window.

id.description: The row's identity: the bill's key (a companion group's primary guid, as the app keys the group's card; a single bill's own plain guid), the action's day and its wording. Only a newer action gives a new id, so a row cleared on the device comes back with it; a change in which member of a group the row shows does not. Opaque: do not parse it.

billGuid.description: The plain guid of the bill the row shows. For a companion group (one row), the member whose status the Bills card shows for the group: a law first, then a veto, a passage, a failure, an update, then the member whose manifest row changed later, then the primary (CompanionGroupIndex.statusLead). The row's number, title, billStatus and vetoed are that member's; its action is the group's latest, from either member.

officialNumber.description: The bill's number as the apps show it: "H.R. 77", "S.J.Res. 213".

title.description: The bill's plain-language headline, as on its bill page.

vetoed.description: Only as true, when the bill's veto stands (billOutcomes.ts deriveBillVetoedFromActions); absent otherwise. billStatus keeps its value.

yourVote.title: RecentActionVoteV1
yourVote.description: The caller's own vote on the bill as the server stores it (on the group's primary when they voted on both members); absent when they only watch it. Never anyone else's.

votedOn.description: The Eastern calendar day the caller's vote was last saved (the vote shown, not the first one), when known.

watched.description: Whether the caller watches the bill (either member of a companion group), by their Watch rows on the server. The Bill row a vote saves has the same key as the bill's Watch row and replaces it, so right after a vote on a watched bill this can be false until the watch is saved again. A client that keeps its own watch state shows that instead.

date.description: The action's day as Congress dates it.

text.description: What happened, in a push's words: "Passed the House", "Became law", "House vote fell short of two-thirds", or Congress's text without record references and a final period.

actionCode.description: The Library of Congress or chamber code of the action, when it has one.

recentActionVoteTiming.title: RecentActionVoteTimingV1
recentActionVoteTiming.description: UX-41 concept 2: how long before a chamber's roll call the caller voted. Present only when the bill (either member of a companion group) has a recorded House or Senate vote inside the window, the latest one, on an Eastern day after the one the caller's vote shown was last saved. Absent when the vote came the same day or later, was changed or saved again on or after that day, or has no time. Describes yourVote: a client showing another vote (one not saved yet) leaves it out.

rollCallDate.description: The roll call's day as Congress dates it.

daysBefore.description: Calendar days from votedOn to rollCallDate.
